analysis.execSummary: Across the whole CM360 upload, $1,003,655 of spend is tied to 38,202 wallet creations ($26.27 each) and 1,653 network connections ($607 each), worth $3.52M CLV — a 3.51× return on attributed activity. The immediate move is inside Meta: in the week of 24 Aug, $1,407 of $2,066 wallet spend sat in ad-sets that produced nothing while the seven-creative Conversions Mass ad-set produced all 264 pooled wallets from $659. This run's payload lost the channel, GA4, universe and feed-quality rails, so channel-level judgements and the period-over-period movement read are unavailable — treat all efficiency figures as directional.
analysis.contentRead: messageThemes was truncated out this run, so message cannot be separated from channel; at ad-set level the Phone Dollars explainer/hack videos (Conversions Mass) earn while the DOSH Earn-1% and $456Offer messages did not this week. A geo-split message holdout between the two themes on the same Meta audience would separate them.
keyFindings: Whole-upload totals: $1,003,655 → 38,202 wallets at $26.27 and 1,653 connections at $607, CLV $3.52M = 3.51× ROI — but walletUniverse was dropped this run, so the attributed share of ALL wallet creations (historically ~40–50%) cannot be verified and these figures describe the tracked subset only.

Meta week 24 Aug (platform workbook rail): $1,406.77 of $2,066.18 wallet spend (68%) produced zero wallets, while the Facebook Conversions Mass ad-set turned $659.41 into 264 pooled wallets at $2.50 — the entire reallocation case rests on this ad-set.

The board's four spending_no_wallets signals are all addressed: Bespoke ($601, 3 creatives) and $456Offer ($126) are the SHIFT action; the two DoshCard ad-sets ($679 combined) are explained by their card-uptake objective, not endorsed as failures — DOSH attribution is less direct and wallets are the wrong yardstick.

Conversions Mass is not a one-week fluke: on creativeBoard (13 weeks, 1 Jun–24 Aug) its campaign's largest row shows $13,172 → 2,509 pooled wallets at $6.91 and 71 connections (~$186 each) against a board benchmark of $21.24/wallet — so the destination rate for the shift should be read as ~$7, not $2.50.

creativeBoard pooledSpendShare is 100% of $67,404 measured spend, and every creativeAssetHash in this week's creative.meta is null — no per-creative wallet, cost or trend claim is permissible anywhere this run; all reads are ad-set grain.

tierSpendSeries: wallet spend was cut ~70% on 1 Jul (from $3.5–3.9k/day to ~$1.0–1.1k/day) yet daily wallets held in the 64–148 range through July — media incrementality on wallet creation is unproven and only a geo media-dark test settles it.

baseCoverage: only 5.5% of 36,940 wallet creators appear in the consumer pay-monthly base export at all (a property of the export, not of media), but 81.2% of those who do appear joined inside the window — connections are ceilinged, not underperforming.

movement is null and channels/campaigns/placements/GA4/feedQuality were truncated: the period-over-period connection read the headline should lead with is unavailable this run, which caps confidence at Low.

CRM overlap: the July refreshed at-risk 60/90-day stim windows (to 6 Sep / 6 Oct) and August High Risk (to 31 Aug) overlap the measured week, and Bill Bonus EDM/SMS landed 1–3 Sep — paid attribution is likely generous around these waves.

widerSpend for wk 24 Aug: wallet media was $4,246 beside $15,456 of device-tier spend (search $14,857, DV360 $598) — that halo onto Phone Dollars is named, not measured; costing it needs the total-spend feed.

whatsWorking.name: Facebook_Conversions_Mass_Native_Wallet-PhoneDollars_GTM_ ad-set (Meta, workbook rail)
whatsWorking.evidence: Wk 24 Aug: $659.41 → 264 pooled wallets ($2.50) across 7 creatives, 1 connection (immature). Multi-week board: campaign rows at $6.91–$11.01/wallet vs $21.24 benchmark, 71 connections at ~$186–244.
whatsWorking.action: Scale: receive the ~$3.1k/mo shifted from the dry ad-sets; hold total Meta wallet budget otherwise and watch cost/wallet for saturation as ad-set spend roughly doubles.

whatsWorking.name: Video format (Meta, wk 24 Aug, workbook rail)
whatsWorking.evidence: formatSpread: $1,469 of video spend carried all 264 wallets at $5.57; $597 of static carried none — flagged actionable by the signal rail.
whatsWorking.action: Hold video-weighted delivery; test statics via a scheduled one-week rotation pause rather than cutting outright.

whatsWasting.name: Static_Static_PhoneDollarsJul-Aug_Bespoke_ + $456Offer_H1_ ad-sets
whatsWasting.evidence: $727.33 combined in wk 24 Aug (Bespoke $600.94 across 3 creatives, $456Offer $126.39), zero wallets; the $456Offer artwork has $4,045 multi-week board spend with zero wallets (board verdict: pooled).
whatsWasting.action: Shift ~$3,150/mo into Conversions Mass; high click rates here (up to 3.3%) are engagement, not efficiency.

whatsWasting.name: PhoneDollars&DoshCard Traffic ad-sets (Reels-Stories + Static)
whatsWasting.evidence: $679.44 in wk 24 Aug, zero wallets (~$2,942/mo run-rate) — but these campaigns target DOSH card uptake, a lagged lead indicator for NZ joins, and wallet attribution is the wrong success metric.
whatsWasting.action: Fix measurement: instrument card-uptake reporting before any budget verdict; do not grade on wallets.

whatsWasting.name: Truncated measurement rails (this run)
whatsWasting.evidence: channels, placements, campaigns, GA4, walletUniverse, feedQuality, weeklyRunRates and movement all absent — $1.00M of spend cannot be ranked or trended.
whatsWasting.action: Restore the full payload before the next flight decision; treat every efficiency figure here as directional.

reallocations.rationale: Source ad-sets spent $727/wk in wk 24 Aug for zero wallets; destination earns $2.50/wallet this week and $6.91–7.63/wallet pooled over 13 board weeks. Sized on the conservative multi-week rate, not the hot week. Connections figure is immature and pooled at ad-set grain.
reallocations.expected: +~105 wallets/wk and +~4 connections/wk at the multi-week pooled rates ($6.91/wallet, ~$186/connection); zero loss at source since its wallet rate is zero.

projection.basisNote: Net uplift uses the destination's multi-week pooled rate from creativeBoard ($6.91/wallet, ~$186/connection on the campaign's largest row) rather than the single measured week's $2.50, minus the source's zero rate. Key risks: rates are platform-attributed only, wallets are ad-set-pooled, and roughly doubling the destination ad-set's spend may saturate its marginal rate.

analysis.incrementalityRead: The channels rail was truncated, so the search-vs-social creating/harvesting split is not measured this run; the standing caution stands that any search/PMax figures harvest intent social creates. The strongest incrementality evidence present — wallets holding through July's ~70% wallet-spend cut — actively questions paid social's marginal contribution and only a geo media-dark settles it.
analysis.funnelRead: GA4 was dropped from this payload (truncated), so no landing→balance leak, click→session ratio, paid-vs-CRM session split, new-vs-existing wallet split or friction read is possible this run; all cost-per-wallet figures may include re-entries. Restore the GA4 rail before pricing the front door.
analysis.crmOverlapRead: The July refreshed at-risk 60- and 90-day stim windows run through 6 Sep and 6 Oct and August High Risk ran to 31 Aug, all overlapping the measured Meta week, with Bill Bonus EDM/SMS on 1–3 Sep. Wallet creations in and after these windows partly belong to CRM, so paid cost-per-wallet is flattered in this period.
analysis.maturationRead: Median days to convert is 5, but tails run to 90: the July cohort (185 connections at d60=d90) and anything tagged in August are floors, not results — do not grade them until late October/November reads. The current-window side of any comparison is always the less mature one.
analysis.creativeRead: On the platform workbook rail (wk 24 Aug), all 264 wallets and the single immature connection belong to the seven-creative Conversions Mass ad-set pool ($659), while $1,407 across the DoshCard, $456Offer and Bespoke ad-sets bought none; video formats carried every wallet, statics none. Engagement disagrees with wallets — the Bespoke videos' 1.5–3.3% click rates produced nothing, so click rate is not a wallet proxy this week.
creativeTests: Geo-split message holdout: run the Phone Dollars explainer message vs the $456Offer/Bespoke device-saving message in separate regions on the same audience — settles whether the message or the ad-set objective explains the zero-wallet weeks without restructuring delivery.
Scheduled format rotation: pause static formats for one week in alternating geos while videos run — settles whether static's $597 zero-wallet week is format failure or pooled-attribution shadow.
testsForNextFlight: Geo media-dark on wallet social for 3–4 weeks: settles whether paid social is incremental at all, given wallets/day held 64–148 through July's ~70% spend cut.

DOSH card-uptake attribution pilot: pipe card acquisitions into the workbook as the DoshCard campaigns' success metric — settles whether the ~$2.9k/mo is earning its stated objective before any budget verdict.

Total-spend halo read: ingest the device/search feed ($15.5k ran beside $4.2k wallet spend in wk 24 Aug) and compare wallet creation in high- vs low-device-spend weeks — settles whether device activity carries a measurable halo onto Phone Dollars.
analysis.dataQualityNotes: STRATEGIC: this payload was truncated — placements, messageThemes, crossChannelFlows, weeklyRunRates, weeklySpendByPaybackTier, campaigns, channels, walletUniverse, GA4 and feedQuality are absent and movement is null, so there is no channel ranking, no universe denominator (attributed share unverifiable), no traffic-quality or new-vs-existing wallet read, and no period-over-period comparison; restore these rails before the next budget decision. DOSH card-uptake outcomes are not instrumented at all despite being those campaigns' objective. DIAGNOSTIC: single wallet-onboarding conversion tag with no click/view-through split in this payload; no reach/frequency data so fatigue cannot be assessed; creativeBoard pooledSpendShare is 100% and 7 creatives share the week's one earning pool, so creative grain exists on Meta only and even there is ad-set-pooled; outsideFeedCoverage is 39 wallet creatives the spend feed cannot see; unplaceableSpend is $26,633 on the board. OPERATIONAL: every creativeAssetHash in creative.meta is null this run and several board rows are artwork_missing ($13,172, $4,557, $2,714, $2,397) — route artwork/tracker hygiene to the agency; it never changes an investment call.

body.content: Media — Wallet / Phone Dollars The page analysis's verdict is Mixed — reallocate (low confidence, driven by maturation coverage and data gaps): wallet media returns 3.7× overall, but $4,990 (67%) of the measured Meta week's $7,493 sat in ad-sets that bought zero wallets, and the highest-dollar action is fixing DoshCard Traffic measurement (~$10,295/mo) to report card uptake rather than wallets — DOSH campaigns target card uptake and DOSH attribution is less direct than other channels, so the "$2,378, zero wallets" read is a measurement issue, not a performance one. - Spend is standing at $9,115 for the last 7 days ($1,302/day, GST-inclusive — not to be grossed up) vs a prior 14-day average of $1,166/day. Data-as-of date is unknown, so this is stated non-temporally. - Wallets and return: whole-upload CM360 shows $1,003,655 spend → 38,357 wallets at $26.17 each, 1,793 matured connections at $560, and $3.71M CLV = 3.7× ROI. Last-7-day wallet creations are not available this run (walletUniverse rail dropped). - Media-attributed network conversions (a subset of wallet creations, not wallet creations themselves) stand at 653 for the last 7 days (93/day vs 126/day prior) at $13.96 per conversion — Wallet-PhoneDollars leads with 394; Meta 354, Search 223 by channel. This rate will only improve as recent wallet cohorts mature — conversion takes up to 30 days from wallet creation (~34% same-day, ~75% by 30 days), so the current figure understates the final outcome and reads as pipeline strength. The fixed-window, same-weekday week-on-week trend is not available this run (weeklyRunRates dropped from the payload). Attach rates and the in-flight wallets-not-yet-connected count are likewise not available this run. - Pipeline health: per the analysis, the pipeline is producing but concentrated — Conversions Mass was the only material producer in the measured week ($2,305 across 7 pooled creatives → 318 wallets at $7.25 pooled). Where the softer raw daily conversion count appears to disagree with the 3.7× verdict, the analysis wins: it reads the full CM360 feed and maturation curve. Best/worst channel and campaign by cost-per-matured-connection cannot be ranked this run (channel and feed-quality rails absent — not measured, not zero). So What — Top 3 Recommendations: - Fix DoshCard Traffic measurement (~$10,295/mo): report card uptake, not wallets — card uptake is the campaign objective and a lead indicator for later NZ joins; never compare DOSH head-to-head on conversion metrics. - Test splitting the 7-creative Conversions Mass ad-set (~$9,982/mo) so wallets resolve per creative — $2,305/wk bought 318 pooled wallets at $7.25, but no per-creative decision is currently possible. - Hold $456Offer on watch (~$8,025/mo) — $4,045 with no wallets this period — and stop and shift to Conversions Mass if dry again; likewise shift the ~$3,285/mo Jul-Aug Bespoke ad-set (zero wallets despite 2.1–2.7% click rates). Cross-report connections: Cross-report connections: the acquisition report shows WIMW prospect creations fell from 238/day to 188/day (-21%) in the same window your attributed conversions fell from 126/day to 93/day (-26%) — independent corroboration of the slowdown in productive media output. Note that acquisition attributes its fall to 'reduced media investment', which your spend figure ($1,302/day, up from $1,166/day) contradicts; your zero-wallet ad-set finding ($4,990 of the $7,493 Meta week) is the better explanation and should be flagged to that reader.
